name: Artabasdos
summary:
Artabasdos or Artavasdos was a Byzantine general of Armenian descent who seized the throne from June 741 until November 743, in usurpation of the reign of Constantine V.

As the son of an Armenian nobleman, Artabasdos rose through the ranks of the Byzantine army to become one of the most powerful generals of his time. His father, Arshak Bagratuni, was a renowned military leader who had fought alongside Emperor Leo III against the Arabs in 734.

Artabasdos's coup against Constantine V took place during a period of great turmoil in the Byzantine Empire, which was facing threats from both within and outside its borders. The empire was also experiencing economic decline and a decline in the power of the imperial court.

Despite his short-lived reign, Artabasdos left a lasting legacy as the founder of the Bagratuni dynasty, which would go on to play a significant role in shaping Armenian history for centuries to come.

As he said 'I am not a usurper, but a liberator' - in an attempt to justify his actions to the people.

His reign also marked a significant turning point in the development of the Byzantine Empire's military tactics and strategies, as he introduced new technologies and innovations that would be adopted by future generals.

In the end, Artabasdos was overthrown after just two years on the throne, but his impact on Armenian history cannot be overstated. He is remembered as a national hero who fought for Armenia's independence against foreign invaders.

He became a symbol of resistance and courage in the face of overwhelming odds - his legacy continues to inspire Armenians to this day.
